rule: Map raw device values to Home Assistant states using enum members exposed by the integration's library rather than magic integers embedded in an entity description.
trigger: An entity description literal contains a state/value mapping keyed by bare integers (e.g. `state_mapping={1000: "standby", 1001: "charging"}`) instead of library enum members.
rationale: Hard-coded protocol constants silently break when the upstream library renumbers or extends its enum; binding to the library's enum makes the breakage a visible import/attribute error instead of a wrong state.

evidence.excerpt: prefer mapping enum members rather than magic integers to avoid silent breakage

rule: Tests must exercise every value declared in an entity description's state mapping, not just the value present in the default fixture.
trigger: A diff adds or extends a `state_mapping`/options dict on an entity description while the accompanying tests only assert the fixture's default value.
rationale: A mapping entry never hit by a test is an untested translation of device data; reviewers treat each declared state as a case the fixtures must drive.

evidence.excerpt: it never exercises the charging (1001) or discharging (1002) mappings

rule: When an entity description's `key` is renamed, update the matching `translation_key` and its `strings.json` entries, or document in a comment why the old translation key is deliberately kept.
trigger: A diff changes the `key=` of an entity description but leaves the adjacent `translation_key=` unchanged.
rationale: A translation key that no longer names the data it describes misleads the next maintainer and hides whether the user-visible string is still accurate.

evidence.excerpt: translation_key is still realtime_command but the underlying key has been changed

rule: Reuse the shared `[%key:common::config_flow::data::*%]` translation references for standard config-flow fields (host, password, ssl, username, port) instead of introducing new literal labels.
trigger: A new or edited `strings.json` config_flow `data` block gives a plain string label for a field that already exists under `common::config_flow::data`.
rationale: Every new literal string enters the translation pipeline and must be maintained and re-translated separately, while the common keys are already translated across all integrations.

evidence.excerpt: Use the shared common translation key for the SSL field label

rule: Every third-party module an integration imports must be declared in that integration's `manifest.json` requirements; do not swap an import to a differently named distribution without updating requirements.
trigger: A diff changes or adds a top-level import of a non-stdlib, non-homeassistant module in `homeassistant/components/<domain>/` without a corresponding `manifest.json` requirements change.
rationale: An undeclared dependency is not installed for that integration, so the module raises ModuleNotFoundError at runtime for every user rather than failing in CI.

evidence.excerpt: if serialx is intentionally required, add it to the integration requirements

rule: A legacy YAML platform reduced to an import/repair-issue stub must still report successful setup - return a no-op service or `True` rather than `None` - so the legacy platform helper does not log a setup failure.
trigger: `async_get_service`, `async_get_scanner` or a comparable legacy platform entry point is rewritten to only create an issue/start an import flow and then return `None`.
rationale: `notify.legacy` and `device_tracker.legacy` interpret a `None` return as failed setup and emit an error-level log on every start, so users see a spurious error alongside the intended repair issue.

evidence.excerpt: consider returning a minimal no-op BaseNotificationService while still creating the repair issue
device_tracker/legacy will treat setup as failed and log an error

rule: Handle the import flow's abort reasons before raising the `deprecated_yaml` repair issue, so a failed import does not tell the user their YAML was successfully migrated.
trigger: A YAML import path calls `async_create_issue(..., translation_key="deprecated_yaml")` unconditionally after starting an import flow, without branching on the flow's abort reason.
rationale: The repair issue is the user's instruction to delete their YAML; issuing it when the import aborted loses their configuration.

evidence.excerpt: handle import abort reasons before creating the deprecated_yaml issue

rule: Do not abort a reconfigure flow on unique-id mismatch when the existing entry still carries the integration's legacy unique_id; match the legacy value and migrate the entry to the new scheme.
trigger: A config flow computes a new-style unique id, calls `async_set_unique_id(...)` and then `_abort_if_unique_id_mismatch()` in the `SOURCE_RECONFIGURE` branch, in a diff that changes how the unique id is derived.
rationale: Existing installs keep the old unique_id until migration runs, so an unconditional mismatch abort permanently blocks reconfigure for every already-installed user after the upgrade.

evidence.excerpt: will abort for existing installs whose config entry unique_id is still the legacy serial number
blocking reconfigure until a reload/restart triggers migration

rule: Never assign to a config flow's `VERSION` or `MINOR_VERSION` at runtime; they are class-level constants describing the entry schema, and migrations must be driven by `async_migrate_entry`.
trigger: A diff contains `self.VERSION = ...` or `self.MINOR_VERSION = ...` inside a config-flow step or handler body.
rationale: Entry schema versions describe the data format, not a per-flow decision; mutating them on the instance makes the stored version depend on which branch a user happened to hit.

evidence.excerpt: I also think we should not modify the constants on runtime

rule: Reserve the `async_`/`_async_` prefix for coroutine functions and callbacks that run on the event loop; rename synchronous helpers to a plain `_setup_*`-style name.
trigger: A diff adds a `def _async_foo(...)`/`def async_foo(...)` that is not `async def` and contains no `await`.
rationale: The prefix is how reviewers judge at a glance whether a call is safe to make from the event loop; a synchronous body behind it hides potential blocking work.

evidence.excerpt: These helpers are synchronous functions but are named with the _async_ prefix

rule: Do not name a variable `platform` when it holds an entity domain such as `switch` or `select`; call it `domain`/`entity_domain` and keep `platform` for the Home Assistant platform concept.
trigger: A loop or parameter named `platform` is assigned entity-domain strings and passed to registry helpers such as entity-unique-id lookups.
rationale: `platform` already has a precise meaning in Home Assistant (the integration providing entities for a domain), so reusing it for the domain makes registry code read backwards.

evidence.excerpt: avoid confusion with Home Assistant "platform" terminology

rule: An entity's state property must read the same field the command method writes; after a successful command, update the entity's own state optimistically and write it rather than waiting for a library field that may not refresh.
trigger: A state property (e.g. `current_option`, `is_on`) reads one library attribute (`last_state`) while `async_select_option`/`async_turn_*` sets a different one (`state`), with no `async_write_ha_state` of the new value.
rationale: If the library does not mirror the setter into the read field, the UI keeps showing the previous value after a successful command and looks broken to the user.

evidence.excerpt: update the entity's current option optimistically after setting the device state (and write it)

rule: Do not zero or clear brightness (or other level attributes) in a light's `async_turn_off`; leave the last level intact so it can be restored on the next turn-on.
trigger: `async_turn_off` in a light platform sets `self._attr_brightness = 0` or otherwise resets a level attribute.
rationale: An off light has no brightness in Home Assistant's model, and discarding the value destroys the level used to restore the light and to seed the next turn-on command.

evidence.excerpt: off devices have no brightness. by setting to 0 you have now lost the brightness

rule: `_handle_coordinator_update` must refresh every entity attribute derived from coordinator data, including the entity name, not just a subset.
trigger: A `_handle_coordinator_update` override assigns some `_attr_*` values from the coordinator payload while other displayed attributes derived from the same payload are left untouched.
rationale: Attributes not refreshed on the coordinator callback stay frozen at their setup-time values, so the entity shows stale device information indefinitely.

evidence.excerpt: Update the entity name when the coordinator data changes (e.g., when the hostname changes)

rule: Do not add per-update lookups that can only ever apply to a subset of devices; gate them behind a setup-time check or cached reference so unaffected devices pay nothing on each update.
trigger: An `available`/update path calls a topology lookup such as `node.get_compose_parent(...)` plus an attribute read on every invocation, unconditionally.
rationale: These paths run on every attribute update for every entity, so work that is meaningless for non-bridge nodes multiplies across the whole device set.

evidence.excerpt: adds work on every update for composed devices that can never have BridgedDeviceBasicInformation.Reachable

rule: Make availability precedence explicit when combining a bridged/composed parent's Reachable with the child endpoint's own: return the parent's verdict directly instead of falling through to the child's attribute.
trigger: An `available` property checks a parent endpoint's `Reachable` attribute and then continues on to read the child endpoint's `Reachable` when the parent is reachable.
rationale: If both endpoints expose the cluster, a stale child value silently overrides a reachable parent, producing inconsistent availability for the same physical device.

evidence.excerpt: Consider returning True directly when the parent reports reachable, to make precedence explicit

rule: When deserializing stored KNX telegram values, accept every payload type the DPT layer can produce (str for DPT 16, dict for DPTComplex) rather than narrowing to numeric/bool types.
trigger: A restore/serialization path filters telegram payloads with `isinstance(value, (int, float, bool))` or a similarly narrow type check.
rationale: KNX datapoint types decode to strings and structured dicts as well as numbers, so a numeric-only filter silently discards valid restored telegram values.

evidence.excerpt: This could be str (DPT 16) or dict (DPTComplex) too?

rule: A change that reroutes an existing device/event action to a new action type must be called out as a behavioral change in the PR description and release notes, even when it is the intended bug fix.
trigger: A diff adds a branch that maps a previously unhandled event type to a new action constant, changing which action existing automations receive.
rationale: Automations users already built against the old fall-through action stop firing, so the change needs to reach them through release notes rather than as a silent regression.

evidence.excerpt: should be documented (and called out in release notes)
